title: The Tortoise and the Hare
author: Aesop
summary: A short fable, used here as a working example of a low-level, low-point title sitting alongside a full novel.

questions.q: Why does the hare agree to the race in the first place?
options: He wants to mock the tortoise for being slow
He has something to prove to a rival hare
questions.why: The race begins as ridicule. The hare is not competing so much as showing off.

questions.q: What does the hare do partway through the race?
questions.why: He is so far ahead that he lies down to sleep, certain he cannot lose.

questions.q: How does the tortoise run the race?
questions.why: The tortoise's whole method is that he does not stop, which is the only reason his slowness stops mattering.

questions.q: What is the moral of the fable?
options: Never make a promise you cannot keep
Steady effort beats talent that is wasted
It is better to be fast than careful
questions.why: The hare has every natural advantage and loses anyway, which is the point the fable is making.

options: He wakes on his own and sees the tortoise near the finish
The tortoise calls out to him
questions.why: He wakes too late and cannot make up the distance, though he runs his fastest.
